newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR PLUNDERS CENTURY AS INDIA WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR PLUNDERS CENTURY AS INDIA WIN.

text.p: Skipper Sachin Tendulkar hit a rapid 117 as India crushed New Zealand by eight wickets in their Independence Cup match on Wednesday.

After New Zealand had struggled to 220 for nine in their 50 overs, Tendulkar and Sourav Ganguly (62) shared an opening partnership of 169 to spur India to an easy win with seven and a half overs remaining.
Cheered on by a crowd of some 60,000 on an easy-paced pitch, Tendulkar was in devastating form and he faced only 136 balls, hitting 13 fours and two sixes.

Tendulkar punished paceman Heath Davis for three off-driven fours and lifted him for a six over midwicket to take 18 runs off one over. He also lofted seamer Gavin Larsen over the ropes at wide mid-off.
Nathan Astle, who was easily New Zealand's best batsman with an 111-ball 92 which included 10 boundaries, had the consolation of bowling Tendulkar when India were five runs short of their target.
New Zealand bowled poorly, none more so than Davis who sent down one erratic over containing 11 deliveries because of wides and no balls and cost 15 runs. His five overs cost 54 runs.
Ganguly, although overshadowed by his captain, was also in good form and his first 16 runs came from boundaries. Altogether he hit eight fours and a six in his 88-ball innings.
The opening stand was broken in the 32nd over, when Ganguly edged Larsen to wicketkeeper Adam Parore.
New Zealand failed to build on to Astle's innings and their run rate slowed after a brisk start as they lost four wickets through run outs.

Astle hit 10 boundaries, including three in one over off medium-pacer Abey Kuruvilla, and was particularly severe on the off-side. It followed his 117 against Pakistan at Mohali in the opening match of the tournament last Friday.
The opener, who survived a difficult chance at mid-off when he was on 52, was eventually bowled by seamer Robin Singh.
India, New Zealand and Pakistan have won one match each in the tournament. New Zealand beat Pakistan last Friday and Sri Lanka lost to Pakistan on Monday.
